text: VASEP urges the Republic of Korea to scrap shrimp import quotas for Việt Nam
HÀ NỘI - The Vietnam Association of Seafood Exporters and Producers (VASEP) has urged the Government to negotiate the removal of quotas on Vietnamese shrimp exported to the Republic of Korea (RoK).
The association says the current quota auction system adds costs equivalent to 14-16 per cent of export value, eroding the benefits of a zero tariff under the bilateral free trade agreement.

In a document sent to the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment and the Ministry of Industry and Trade, the association called for the issue to be prioritised in consultations and negotiations to review and upgrade the Vietnam-RoK Free Trade Agreement (VKFTA).
Under the agreement, the RoK allows 15,000 tonnes of Vietnamese shrimp a year to enter this market at a zero import tariff.
However, the quota is allocated through an auction system requiring businesses to pay additional costs to access this quota.
According to feedback from companies compiled by VASEP, these costs amount to around 14-16 per cent of export value from Việt Nam to the Republic of Korea.
Meanwhile, shrimp exported outside the quota face a 20 per cent tariff.
This raises product prices and weakens their competitiveness.
The association said the system also discouraged Korean buyers from increasing purchases of Vietnamese shrimp to benefit from the VKFTA.
Some businesses are considering switching to alternative suppliers, including Peru.

VASEP has proposed that the Ministry of Industry and Trade, in coordination with the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment, prioritise negotiations to apply a zero import tariff without volume restrictions to shrimp product lines covered by the agreement.

The move would allow exporters and importers to make fuller use of tariff preferences, reduce import costs for Korean partners and help maintain the competitiveness of Vietnamese shrimp, the association said.
The Republic of Korea remains one of Việt Nam's key seafood export markets.
According to VASEP, Việt Nam's seafood reached US$864 million in 2025, up 7.2 per cent from the previous year.
In the first nine months of 2026, the exports rose 5.6 per cent year on year to $649.1 million.
Shrimp and mollusc were the two leading product groups, generating $262.5 million and $234 million, respectively.
The Republic of Korea imports more than 100,000 tonnes of shrimp annually, worth an estimated $800 million to $1 billion.
Vietnamese shrimp accounts for nearly 50 per cent of imports, supported by the VKFTA despite the existing quota restrictions, VASEP said.
Việt Nam imported $49.6 million worth of seafood from the Republic of Korea during the same period, down 24.5 per cent year on year.
Other fish accounted for the largest share at $37.5 million, followed by tuna at $7.2 million.
VASEP said the VKFTA had provided a favourable framework for bilateral seafood trade, helping businesses access the Korean market and benefit from tariff preferences.
However, the exporters continue to face technical barriers, stringent food safety requirements, traceability rules and demands for supply chain transparency.
Competition and quota mechanisms for certain products also limit their ability to benefit fully from the agreement.

The association also called on relevant ministries and agencies to assess the two-way impact of potential VKFTA upgrades on bilateral seafood trade, ensure balanced benefits and avoid imposing unnecessary compliance requirements on businesses. - VNS
